candidates.title: 이분 탐색
candidates.concept_granularity: single method of finding a value in sorted data by comparing against the middle and discarding the half that cannot contain it - the next bounds moving past the middle rather than to it, since leaving it in loops forever - which is logarithmic on sorted input and costs the sort itself when the input is not

candidates.title: 이진 탐색 트리
candidates.concept_granularity: single ordering imposed on a binary tree - everything in a node's left subtree is smaller than it and everything in the right is larger - from which it follows that the smallest value is the leftmost node and the largest the rightmost

candidates.title: 이진탐색트리에서 노드 지우기
candidates.concept_granularity: single procedure split by how many children the node has - a leaf is simply unreferenced, a node with one child has the reference to it redirected at that child, and a node with two is replaced by the smallest value in its right subtree or equally the largest in its left - with a search having to find the node first in every case

candidates.title: 전위 순회와 후위 순회
candidates.concept_granularity: single pair of traversals differing from the inorder one only in when the node itself is visited - before both subtrees or after both of them

candidates.title: 이진탐색트리의 시간복잡도
candidates.concept_granularity: single spread across the three cases - constant when the node wanted is the root, logarithmic on average because each comparison discards one side and halves what is left, and linear at worst when the tree has degenerated into a line

candidates.title: 큐
candidates.concept_granularity: single restricted structure in which what entered first leaves first - additions at the back, reads and removals at the front, each in constant time, which is the whole of its interface

candidates.title: 스택
candidates.concept_granularity: single structure allowing insertion and removal at one end only, so the last thing in is the first out - one of the restricted structures alongside the queue and the deque - and although the underlying array could be read at any position, doing so is outside what the structure offers, since the problems it solves need only push, pop and a look at the top

candidates.title: 배열과 큐로 서로를 흉내내기
candidates.concept_granularity: single pair of substitutions - an array cannot stand in for the first-in-first-out structure because removing at the front shifts everything, which is what the linked structure avoids; and two of the queues make a stack, everything but the last entry being moved across before it is taken out

candidates.title: 합병 정렬
candidates.concept_granularity: single divide-and-conquer sort that splits the array into two equal halves, sorts each the same way and merges the results - log-linear in every case including the worst, which is what distinguishes it from the other advanced sort - at the price of memory for the merge, which is the reason to prefer the other when memory is what matters

candidates.title: JIT 컴파일러
candidates.concept_granularity: single run-time bytecode-to-machine-code translation strategy that caches and reuses generated code

locators.heading: # Chapter 01 - 자바 프로그래밍 > ## Java 특징 > ### 01. 플랫폼(프로그램이 실행되는 환경)에 영향을 받지 않음

candidates.title: 이진탐색트리의 장단점
candidates.concept_granularity: single balance of what the structure buys and costs - insertion and deletion move references rather than elements, the ordering makes all three operations fast in the usual case, and the values can be read out in order - against the one failure mode, a tree that has leaned to one side, which is what the self-balancing variants exist to prevent

candidates.title: 분할 정복
candidates.concept_granularity: single strategy underlying much else - cut the problem into smaller problems of the same shape, solve each the same way until one is small enough to answer outright, and build the answer from theirs; three steps that the merging sort shows most plainly

candidates.title: 절반씩 줄면 로그다
candidates.concept_granularity: single identification worth carrying - any procedure that discards half the remaining data per step is logarithmic, because halving n down to one takes as many steps as the exponent that raises two to n; and that number is small enough to treat as constant, ten million taking twenty-four steps

candidates.title: 탐색 트리의 최소와 최대
candidates.concept_granularity: single consequence of the ordering - going left as far as possible reaches the smallest value and going right as far as possible reaches the largest, so neither needs searching for

candidates.title: 스택 두 개로 큐 만들기
candidates.concept_granularity: single construction turning two last-in-first-out structures into a first-in-first-out one - everything entering goes on the first, and anything leaving comes off the second, which is refilled by pouring the first into it whenever it runs dry; the pouring reverses the order, which is exactly what was wanted

candidates.title: 컴파일러
aliases: 소스 코드 전체를 한 번에 번역
candidates.concept_granularity: single program that translates a whole source text into machine code before any of it runs, producing a separate executable - which makes translating slow and running fast, the opposite of the line-at-a-time translator that produces no executable at all and re-reads the source every run

candidates.title: 프론트엔드와 백엔드
candidates.concept_granularity: single division of the translator into two halves - the first understanding the source language and knowing nothing about any machine, the second emitting for a machine and knowing nothing about any language - which is what lets one language be retargeted and one machine serve many languages

candidates.title: 어휘 분석기
candidates.concept_granularity: single first stage that turns the source text into a sequence of tokens, each an integer the rest of the translator can work with rather than a run of characters - a conditional and its parenthesised comparison becoming six of them

candidates.title: 구문 분석기
candidates.concept_granularity: single second stage that checks the token sequence against the language's grammar - reporting an error where it does not fit and otherwise emitting the program's structure as a tree, which is what every later stage works on

candidates.title: 중간 코드 생성과 의미 검사
candidates.concept_granularity: single third stage that checks what the grammatically valid program actually means - assigning a fractional value to an integer being the standard example of something the grammar permits and the meaning forbids - and emits a machine-independent form of it

candidates.title: 최적화 단계
candidates.concept_granularity: single optional stage that rewrites the intermediate form into something cheaper - chiefly faster and secondarily smaller - bound by three conditions: the meaning must not change, the average case must actually improve, and the rewriting must be worth what it costs to do

candidates.title: 지역 최적화와 전역 최적화
candidates.concept_granularity: single split between rewrites needing only a local look - folding constants the compiler can compute itself, dropping repeated loads and stores, simplifying algebra, replacing an expensive operation with a cheaper equivalent - and rewrites needing to trace how values flow through the whole program, which is what finds a repeated subexpression, a computation that does not change inside a loop, or code nothing can reach

candidates.title: 목적 코드 생성기
candidates.concept_granularity: single last stage turning the machine-independent form into actual instructions - which means choosing them, deciding what lives in which register, laying out storage, and applying whatever further improvement only makes sense once the machine is known

candidates.title: 컴파일 오류 처리
candidates.concept_granularity: single set of duties around an error - noticing it, containing it so the rest of the program is still checked rather than drowned in consequences, reporting it, and in some translators attempting a fix - across the three kinds that arise, the grammatical, the meaningful, and the one that appears only when the program runs

candidates.title: 단일 패스와 다중 패스
candidates.concept_granularity: single trade in how many times the source is walked - once is fastest and was what the early translators did, while several times allows each stage to be improved on its own, makes retargeting to another machine easier and needs less memory at any moment, at the cost of taking longer
